issues.description: No introduction explaining what file type filtering is and why it's useful
issues.should_add: Explain that file types let you filter by language/format (e.g., search only Rust files, exclude JavaScript). More convenient than globs for common cases.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add intro section: 'File type filtering allows you to search specific file types by language or format. Instead of using glob patterns, you can use predefined types like "rust", "python", or "markdown". Ripgrep ships with 150+ built-in file types and supports custom type definitions.'

issues.description: No documentation of the -t/--type flag for selecting file types
issues.should_add: Document -t/--type flag usage with examples. Show that multiple -t flags can be combined. Mention -t can be used in short form like -trust.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section with examples:
```bash
# Search only Rust files
rg pattern -t rust

# Search Python and JavaScript files
rg TODO -t python -t js

# Short form: -trust is same as -t rust
rg error -trust
```
Explain that --type has lower precedence than --glob and ignore files.

issues.description: No documentation of the -T/--type-not flag for excluding file types
issues.should_add: Document -T/--type-not for excluding file types. Show it can be combined with -t for complex filtering.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section with examples:
```bash
# Search all files EXCEPT JavaScript
rg pattern -T js

# Search Rust but not test files
rg TODO -t rust -T test

# Exclude multiple types
rg FIXME -T js -T css -T html
```
Mention that -T can use short form like -Trust.

issues.description: No documentation of --type-list flag for discovering available types
issues.should_add: Document --type-list flag and show example output format. Explain that it shows all built-in types plus any custom types defined via --type-add.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section:
```bash
# List all available file types
rg --type-list

# Example output:
ada: *.adb, *.ads
rust: *.rs
python: *.py, *.pyi, *.pyw
javascript: *.js, *.jsx, *.mjs
...
```
Explain format: type_name: glob1, glob2, ...

issues.description: No documentation of --type-add for defining custom file types
issues.should_add: Document --type-add syntax for creating custom types. Show basic glob syntax and include directive for composing types.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add comprehensive section:
```bash
# Define custom type with single glob
rg --type-add 'foo:*.foo' -t foo pattern

# Define type with multiple extensions
rg --type-add 'web:*.{html,css,js}' -t web TODO

# Compose type from existing types using include:
rg --type-add 'src:include:cpp,py,rust' -t src FIXME

# Combine include with additional globs
rg --type-add 'config:include:json,yaml' --type-add 'config:*.conf' -t config
```
Note: Type names must be alphanumeric (letters and numbers only, no punctuation).
Note: Settings not persisted - use config file for permanent definitions.

issues.description: No documentation of --type-clear for removing default globs
issues.should_add: Document --type-clear for clearing built-in type definitions before adding custom ones.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section:
```bash
# Clear built-in rust type and define your own
rg --type-clear rust --type-add 'rust:*.rs' -t rust pattern

# Useful for overriding default definitions
rg --type-clear c --type-add 'c:*.c' -t c TODO
```
Explain: Clears globs for specified type, allowing clean override. Can still add globs after clearing.

issues.description: No documentation of special 'all' type value
issues.should_add: Document that --type=all enables whitelist mode (only search recognized types), and --type-not=all enables blacklist mode (only search unrecognized files).
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section:
```bash
# Search only files with recognized types (whitelist mode)
rg --type all pattern

# Search only files WITHOUT recognized types (blacklist mode)
rg --type-not all pattern
```
Explain whitelist/blacklist modes and when they're useful.

issues.description: No reference list of the 150+ built-in file types
issues.should_add: Include a reference table or appendix showing commonly used built-in types. Direct users to --type-list for complete list.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section listing popular types:

Commonly used built-in types:
- Programming: rust, python, go, java, javascript, typescript, c, cpp, ruby, php
- Web: html, css, json, yaml, xml
- Documentation: markdown, rst, asciidoc
- Config: config, toml, ini
- Build: make, cmake, gradle

For complete list with glob patterns, run: rg --type-list

See also: crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs for all 150+ definitions.

issues.description: No practical real-world examples showing common use cases
issues.should_add: Add practical examples section showing common workflows
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add examples:
```bash

rg TODO -t rust -t python -t go

# Search config files for a setting
```

issues.description: No explanation of how --type interacts with --glob and ignore files
issues.should_add: Explain that --type has lower precedence than --glob and ignore files
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note: Type filtering has lower precedence than glob patterns (--glob) and ignore files (.gitignore, etc.). If a file is excluded by an ignore file, --type won't include it. Use explicit file paths or --no-ignore to override.

issues.description: No mention of using configuration files to persist type definitions
issues.should_add: Note that type settings can be persisted in configuration files
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add note: Since --type-add settings aren't persisted across invocations, consider adding them to a ripgrep configuration file (see Configuration chapter). Example config:
```
--type-add
web:*.{html,css,js}
--type-add
config:include:json,yaml,toml
```

issues.description: No technical explanation of how type matching is implemented
issues.should_add: Brief explanation of how types map to glob patterns under the hood
issues.fix_suggestion: Add technical note: File types are implemented as named collections of glob patterns. When you use -t rust, ripgrep internally uses the glob *.rs to match files. The TypesBuilder creates a GlobSet for efficient matching. See crates/ignore/src/types.rs for implementation details.
